notes.summary: Handwritten page 66 defines cosupport and support, gives a braced relation with two marginal notes, then defines saturated parts. A heavily cancelled draft lies between the first definitions and the live Donc. All connected graphic enclosures are represented in TikZ.
notes.math_reading_decisions: No mathematical proof or computation was used. Direct ink comparison distinguished one-p cosup from two-p cosupp/supp and member F from family F. Formula structure drew attention to the first upright-and-tick relation, the low dot, the bottom F bar and the surprising final support; none was normalized to an expected mathematical statement.
notes.author_checks: No authorial proof check or explicit correction of a theorem is asserted. The bottom phrase is copied as “cosupport de son support”, despite the preceding family definition using cosupport twice. Cancelled and overwritten groups are retained, with uncertainty where their letters or state remain obscured.
notes.title_dates_pagination: Manuscript page number 66 at top centre; scan 67 retained. No date or separate title. “Partie saturée … de” is underlined in the first lower definition. No cote marker has been added.

workflow_feedback: The prescribed crop width is useful, but cancellation blocks containing several tightly adjacent uncertain groups need a single wider crop; independently recropping each glyph would overlap the same evidence. This run used 16 locus-cluster crops and never recropped a decided place.
The report schema should specify whether change_c and change_h are booleans; this report uses booleans. All bbox values explicitly name the source with bbox_image.

Context limitation: the tight crops 03 and 09 show their target row and immediate nearby strokes/whitespace but not a complete adjacent text line. Their surrounding layout had already been read in the supplied half. They were not recropped after decision.
